title: North Island vs South Island for Families — Which to Choose First?
meta_desc: North Island vs South Island for families: compare activity density, drive times, and costs
intro: When planning a family trip to New Zealand, the choice between the North and South Islands can be overwhelming, with both offering unique experiences like visiting Hobbiton Movie Set in Matamata for $89 per adult and $44 per child, or hiking the famous Routeburn Track. With varying activity densities, drive times, and costs, it's essential to weigh your options carefully. For instance, driving from Auckland to Rotorua takes around 3 hours, while Queenstown to Wanaka takes approximately 1 hour.

sections.heading: Activity Density and Variety
sections.body: The North Island is home to a higher population density and more urban centers, which translates to a wider range of activities and attractions, such as the Auckland Sky Tower ($32 per adult, $16 per child) and the Te Puia thermal reserve in Rotorua ($50 per adult, $25 per child). In contrast, the South Island offers more expansive natural landscapes and outdoor activities, like skiing in Queenstown and hiking in Abel Tasman National Park.

sections.heading: Drive Times and Logistics
list: Wellington to Auckland: 8 hours with ferry crossing

sections.heading: Age and Interests
sections.body: Families with younger children might prefer the North Island for its more abundant kid-friendly attractions, such as the Auckland Zoo ($25 per adult, $13 per child) and the theme park Rainbow's End in Auckland ($62 per person). Older children and teenagers may enjoy the more adventurous activities offered in the South Island, like bungee jumping in Queenstown ($205 per person) or white-water rafting in Franz Josef ($120 per person).

sections.heading: What You Miss If You Only Do One Island
list: North Island exclusives: Hobbiton Movie Set, Bay of Islands, East Cape
South Island exclusives: Milford Sound, Mount Cook, Franz Josef Glacier
